segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome back to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: And my name is Catherine and today we have a very scary story.
segments.zh: 我的名字是凯瑟琳，今天我们有一个非常可怕的故事。

segments.en: Spooky.
segments.zh: 诡异的。

segments.en: We're actually bringing you the first of our advanced media lessons and what better way to start it with than a scary story for Halloween.
segments.zh: 这是我们的第一期高级听力素材课程，用一个万圣节恐怖故事来开场，再合适不过了。

segments.en: Than with.
segments.zh: 比与。

segments.en: Than with.
segments.zh: 比与。

segments.en: So what better way to start this advanced media lesson than with a scary story.
segments.zh: 那么，有什么比恐怖故事更好的方式来开始这个高级媒体课程了。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So Halloween is coming up and advanced media usually features a new story or some kind of story that we can then kind of break down and talk about.
segments.zh: 万圣节快到了。高级听力素材课程通常会选一则新闻或某个故事，然后我们一起分析、讨论。

segments.en: Just have a conversation about because you're advanced level learners and you want to have fun with English.
segments.zh: 我们就围绕它聊一聊，因为你们已经是高级英语学习者，也希望享受使用英语的乐趣。

segments.en: So where is today's spooky story set Marco?
segments.zh: 那么，今天这个诡异的故事发生在哪里呢，Marco？

segments.en: Well it starts out with a guy who remembers something very scary that happened to him when he was a kid.
segments.zh: 故事一开始，一个男人回忆起自己小时候经历过的一件非常可怕的事。

segments.en: Okay and so one of the main characters in today's story is his great aunt.
segments.zh: 好的，所以今天故事里的主要人物之一就是他的姑婆。

segments.en: That's right his great aunt.
segments.zh: 没错，他的姑婆。

segments.en: And so basically this is a family member but it's your father's aunt.
segments.zh: 所以基本上她是家庭成员，是你父亲的姑妈。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Your grandmother or your grandfather's sister.
segments.zh: 你的祖母或你祖父的妹妹。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Alright so your aunt or your aunt is your parent's sibling.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以你的阿姨或阿姨是你父母的兄弟姐妹。

segments.en: But in this case we're talking about one generation older than that.
segments.zh: 但在这种情况下，我们谈论的是比这更老的一代。

segments.en: So you could say great aunt, great uncle, great grandfather, great grandmother.
segments.zh: 所以你可以说姑婆、叔公、曾祖父、曾祖母。

segments.en: It's like one step back.
segments.zh: 这就像一步后退。

segments.en: So this is usually a very old person and the great aunt is definitely an important character in today's story.
segments.zh: 所以，这通常指一位年纪很大的长辈，而这位姑婆显然是今天故事里的重要人物。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So let's not keep you in suspense any longer.
segments.zh: 那我们就不卖关子了。

segments.en: Why don't we listen to this scary story and we'll be right back to talk about it.
segments.zh: 我们为什么不听这个可怕的故事，我们会马上回来谈论它。

segments.en: Oh no the lights went out.
segments.zh: 糟了，灯灭了。

segments.en: Honey can you light a candle?
segments.zh: 亲爱的，你能点燃蜡烛吗？

segments.en: Sure.
segments.zh: 当然。

segments.en: What do we do now?
segments.zh: 我们现在该怎么办？

segments.en: Well we can just talk you know like we used to.
segments.zh: 我们可以聊聊天啊，就像以前那样。

segments.en: I know.
segments.zh: 我知道。

segments.en: I'll tell you a scary story.
segments.zh: 我会告诉你一个可怕的故事。

segments.en: It happened to me and my dad when I was a teenager.
segments.zh: 当我十几岁的时候，它发生在我和我的父亲身上。

segments.en: I was living with my father at the time when he received a phone call.
segments.zh: 当时他接到电话，我和父亲住在一起。

segments.en: Hello.
segments.zh: 你好。

segments.en: Yes this is him.
segments.zh: 对，我就是。

segments.en: I see.
segments.zh: 我明白了。

segments.en: Sorry to hear that.
segments.zh: 很遗憾听到这个消息。

segments.en: Okay no problem.
segments.zh: 好吧没问题。

segments.en: I'll be there shortly.
segments.zh: 我很快就会到那里。

segments.en: Pack some clothes Tony.
segments.zh: 收拾一些衣服，托尼。

segments.en: My great aunt is very ill and no one in the family wants to take care of her.
segments.zh: 我的姑婆病得很重，家里又没人愿意照顾她。

segments.en: We're going to stay at her house for a few days.
segments.zh: 我们要在她家住几天。

segments.en: Aunt?
segments.zh: 姑婆？

segments.en: What aunt?
segments.zh: 什么姑婆？

segments.en: I never knew you had a great aunt.
segments.zh: 我从来不知道你还有位姑婆。

segments.en: Well the family doesn't talk about her or get near her for that matter.
segments.zh: 家里人从不提她，甚至都不愿意接近她。

segments.en: Why is that?
segments.zh: 为什么会这样？

segments.en: Come on we have to go.
segments.zh: 来吧，我们得走了。

segments.en: So we arrived at this old house on the outskirts of our town.
segments.zh: 所以我们到达了我们镇郊区的这座老房子。

segments.en: There was almost no one around and the house had an eerie look to it.
segments.zh: 周围几乎没有人，房子的外观令人毛骨悚然。

segments.en: Once inside the house we walked to her room and I was surprised to find my dad's great aunt in a wheelchair yelling at someone but we were alone in the room.
segments.zh: 进屋后，我们走向她的房间。我惊讶地发现，爸爸的姑婆坐在轮椅上，对着什么人大喊，可房间里明明只有我们。

segments.en: Hi Aunt Ursula.
segments.zh: 厄休拉姑婆，您好。

segments.en: This is my son Tony.
segments.zh: 这是我的儿子托尼。

segments.en: Why have you come?
segments.zh: 你为什么来？

segments.en: Why are you here?
segments.zh: 你为什么在这里？

segments.en: Don't you know it isn't safe?
segments.zh: 你不知道这不安全吗？

segments.en: My time is near.
segments.zh: 我的大限快到了。

segments.en: He's coming for me.
segments.zh: 他来找我了。

segments.en: Who is coming for you?
segments.zh: 谁来接你？

segments.en: The Prince of Darkness.
segments.zh: 黑暗之王。

segments.en: The Lord of the Underworld.
segments.zh: 冥界之主。

segments.en: The Tempter.
segments.zh: 诱惑者。

segments.en: The Old Serpent.
segments.zh: 老蛇。

segments.en: Come on.
segments.zh: 来吧。

segments.en: Aunt Ursula let's lay you down.
segments.zh: 厄休拉姑婆，我们扶您躺下吧。

segments.en: You need to get some rest.
segments.zh: 你需要休息一下。

segments.en: Tony help me lay her down.
segments.zh: 托尼，帮我扶她躺下。

segments.en: That night we slept in one of the 12 rooms of that big old mansion.
segments.zh: 那天晚上，我们睡在那座大豪宅的 12 个房间之一。

segments.en: The trees outside seemed to come alive and their shadows formed ghoulish shapes on my bed.
segments.zh: 屋外的树仿佛活了过来，树影投到我的床上，形成一个个鬼怪般的轮廓。

segments.en: All of a sudden we heard screaming.
segments.zh: 突然间，我们听到尖叫声。

segments.en: Ahhh! Get off me, beast! I won't let you take me! Ahhh! Dad! Dad! Something is attacking Aunt Ursula! Take your claws off me! Go back to the underworld, you demon! I shall be judged before you can take me! The door is jammed! Stand back!
segments.zh: 啊！放开我，你这野兽！我不会让你把我带走！啊！爸爸！爸爸！有什么东西在袭击厄休拉姑婆！把你的爪子拿开！滚回地狱去，你这恶魔！在你带走我之前，我必须先接受审判！门卡住了！退后！

segments.en: Aunt Ursula where are you?
segments.zh: 厄休拉姑婆，您在哪儿？

segments.en: Over here!
segments.zh: 在这里！

segments.en: And as we approached her she was lying on the floor with her hands and feet open like the Vitruvian Man, breathing heavily with bloody marks and scratches on her arms, legs and face.
segments.zh: 我们走近她时，她躺在地板上，四肢像《维特鲁威人》那样张开，喘着粗气，胳膊、腿和脸上满是带血的痕迹和抓伤。

segments.en: Remember how I mentioned that she was in a wheelchair?
segments.zh: 还记得我提到她坐在轮椅上吗？

segments.en: My aunt had been paralyzed from the neck down for just over a year.
segments.zh: 我的姑婆颈部以下瘫痪，已经有一年多了。

segments.en: After this incident, strange things would happen in the house and my aunt would yell and scream, according to her, warding off the evil that had come to get her.
segments.zh: 这件事之后，屋子里开始发生怪事，我的姑婆会大喊大叫。按她的说法，是在驱赶前来抓她的邪恶力量。

segments.en: As the days passed, she became very weak and eventually was unable to talk.
segments.zh: 日子过去了，她变得非常虚弱，最终无法说话。

segments.en: My dad had to work during the day, so I was left to care for her.
segments.zh: 我爸爸白天要上班，所以我只能照顾她。

segments.en: When she lost her voice and laid on her deathbed, I would hear her breathe in and out.
segments.zh: 她失去声音、躺在临终的病床上时，我能听见她一呼一吸的声音。

segments.en: Until finally one day, she breathed in and never exhaled.
segments.zh: 直到最后有一天，她吸了口气，从未呼气。

segments.en: That night, I felt relieved that it was finally over, but it wasn't.
segments.zh: 那天晚上，我松了一口气，终于结束了，但事实并非如此。

segments.en: I was so terrified of what I was hearing that I didn't sleep all night.
segments.zh: 那些声音把我吓坏了，我一整夜都没睡。

segments.en: The following morning, I went to the bathroom, expecting to find a mess and everything torn up, but I found everything exactly as it was before.
segments.zh: 第二天早上，我走进浴室，本以为里面会一片狼藉，东西都被撕毁了，却发现一切都和原来一模一样。

segments.en: The movers came that same day and as we were cleaning out her drawers and personal items, we found strange notebooks with names and amounts of money written next to them.
segments.zh: 搬家工人当天就来了。我们清理她的抽屉和私人物品时，发现了一些奇怪的笔记本，上面写着一些名字，旁边还有金额。

segments.en: We found pictures with people's faces sewn with black or red string.
segments.zh: 我们还发现了一些照片，照片上的人脸被黑线或红线缝过。

segments.en: And you want to know what the strangest thing was?
segments.zh: 你想知道最奇怪的事情是什么吗？

segments.en: There was a small doll filled with dead ants, with a strand of hair tied around its waist.
segments.zh: 有一个装满死蚂蚁的小娃娃，腰间系着一缕头发。

segments.en: And on the doll's face, there was a picture of me with the numbers 31-10-09.
segments.zh: 在娃娃的脸上，有一张我的照片，数字是 31-10-09。

segments.en: You know what date it is today?
segments.zh: 你知道今天是什么日期吗？

segments.en: October 31st, 2009.
Alright, we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So, what did you think?
segments.zh: 那么，你怎么看？

segments.en: Pretty scary?
segments.zh: 很吓人？

segments.en: I got goosebumps.
segments.zh: 我起鸡皮疙瘩。

segments.en: It's a little spooky.
segments.zh: 这有点吓人。

segments.en: A little scary.
segments.zh: 有点吓人。

segments.en: Now, what's interesting about this story, it's based on a true story, so that makes it even scarier.
segments.zh: 这个故事有意思的地方在于，它是根据真实经历改编的，所以就更吓人了。

segments.en: No.
segments.zh: 不。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Dare I ask, did this happen to you?
segments.zh: 我敢问，这发生在你身上吗？

segments.en: No, no.
segments.zh: 不，不。

segments.en: I'm not old enough, but this actually happened to a family member of mine, and that's why I know this story.
segments.zh: 我还没有那么大年纪，不过这件事确实发生在我的一位家人身上，所以我才知道这个故事。

segments.en: So, it was kind of told to me when I was a bit younger and I remembered it.
segments.zh: 这件事是在我小一点的时候别人讲给我听的，我一直记着。

segments.en: And well, Halloween is a great time to remember these things.
segments.zh: 好吧，万圣节是记住这些事情的好时机。

segments.en: And the first time you heard it, it scared the crap out of you, right?
segments.zh: 第一次听到的时候，把你吓坏了，对吧？

segments.en: Oh yeah, for sure.
segments.zh: 哦，是的，当然。

segments.en: Actually, the first time I heard it, we were on an airplane, like on October 31st.
segments.zh: 其实我第一次听这个故事时，我们正在飞机上，就在 10 月 31 日那天。

segments.en: Oh wow.
segments.zh: 哦，哇。

segments.en: So, it was pretty scary.
segments.zh: 所以，这很可怕。

segments.en: Well, we've got a lot of really interesting stuff here.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们这里有很多非常有趣的东西。

segments.en: We're not going to dwell too long on the grammar or the vocabulary because we assume that most of you have understood this, but there are a couple of things that can be really difficult even for English speakers.
segments.zh: 我们不会在语法或词汇上停留太久，因为相信大多数人已经听懂了，但其中有几处，连英语母语者也可能觉得难。

segments.en: So, the first one is this phrase, my time is near.
segments.zh: 所以，第一个就是这句话，我的时间快到了。

segments.en: My time is near.
segments.zh: 我的时间快到了。

segments.en: So, what does that mean exactly?
segments.zh: 那么，这究竟意味着什么？

segments.en: Well, my time is near, my end is coming.
segments.zh: 好吧，我的时间快到了，我的结局即将到来。

segments.en: It means I'm very old and I'm probably going to die soon.
segments.zh: 这意味着我很老了，我可能很快就会死去。

segments.en: So my time, his time, that's when you die.
segments.zh: 所以我的时间，他的时间，那是你死的时候。

segments.en: Okay, so it's always used in reference to death, right?
segments.zh: 好吧，所以它总是用来指代死亡，对吧？

segments.en: In this case, yeah.
segments.zh: 在这种情况下，是的。

segments.en: So, it's used in reference to death and in this case, we have the aunt who's talking about herself, but you could also say his time is coming, we should visit him in the hospital.
segments.zh: 所以，这个说法与死亡有关。故事里是姑婆在说自己，但你也可以说：“他的时日不多了，我们应该去医院看看他。”

segments.en: So, it's a kind of softer way of saying that someone is going to die soon.
segments.zh: 所以，这是一种更温和的说法，有人很快就会死去。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Okay, so my time is near or his time is near.
segments.zh: 好的，所以我的时间快到了，或者他的时间快到了。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And then, something really interesting in this story as well, she had many different names that she called the devil.
segments.zh: 这个故事还有一个很有意思的地方：她用了许多不同的称呼来指代魔鬼。

segments.en: So, she didn't directly say the devil, she said the prince of darkness.
segments.zh: 所以，她没有直接说魔鬼，她说的是黑暗之王。

segments.en: Prince of darkness, lord of the underworld, the tempter.
segments.zh: 黑暗之王，冥界之王，试探者。

segments.en: The tempter and the old serpent.
segments.zh: 诱惑者和老蛇。

segments.en: So, these are actually different ways that historically have been used to describe the devil, right?
segments.zh: 所以，这些其实都是历史上用来称呼魔鬼的不同说法，对吧？

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And a lot of them are biblical, like the old serpent, you know, back in the first pages of the Bible when the serpent tempts Eve, that's the devil.
segments.zh: 很多说法都出自《圣经》，比如“古蛇”。《圣经》开头讲到那条引诱夏娃的蛇，那就是魔鬼。

segments.en: And so, we hear a lot of these, especially on Halloween, these are great words to use to kind of diversify and not say devil, devil, devil.
segments.zh: 所以，这些称呼我们经常会听到，尤其是在万圣节。用它们能让表达更多样，不必一直重复“魔鬼、魔鬼、魔鬼”。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So, apart from those synonyms for the devil, she also used an interesting phrase towards the end when she said, I shall be judged before you can take me.
segments.zh: 除了这些魔鬼的同义称呼，她在故事快结束时还用了一个有意思的说法：“在你带走我之前，我必须先接受审判。”

segments.en: Hmm.
segments.zh: 嗯。

segments.en: So, judged, to judge, this is to see if something is right or wrong.
segments.zh: 所以，判断，判断，这是为了看某事是对还是错。

segments.en: But in this case, we talk about judgment at the end of a person's life.
segments.zh: 但在这里，我们说的是一个人生命终结时的审判。

segments.en: So, that means when you go to the gates of heaven and there's Saint Peter and he has a list of the good and the bad and he says yes or no.
segments.zh: 意思就是，你来到天堂之门，圣彼得在那里，手里有一份记录善恶的名单，由他来决定你能不能进去。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: And then if you're a no, you get sent down to hell.
segments.zh: 然后，如果你是一个不，你会被送入地狱。

segments.en: If you're a yes, you go to heaven.
segments.zh: 如果你是一个，你就去天堂。

segments.en: So, she says, I shall be judged.
segments.zh: 所以，她说，我将被审判。

segments.en: This means, I want my day in court.
segments.zh: 意思是：我要在法庭上为自己申辩。

segments.en: I want to have my actions analyzed by Saint Peter, not by you.
segments.zh: 我想让圣彼得分析我的行为，而不是你。

segments.en: Right, exactly.
segments.zh: 对，没错。

segments.en: So, actually, this makes reference to a lot of beliefs in Christianity, right?
segments.zh: 所以，实际上，这提到了许多对基督教的信仰，对吧？

segments.en: So, it's just another aspect of the story.
segments.zh: 所以，这只是故事的另一个方面。

segments.en: But of course, other religions probably don't have the same things such as the gates of heaven and Saint Peter.
segments.zh: 当然，其他宗教未必也有天堂之门、圣彼得这样的概念。

segments.en: Right, the system of judgment.
segments.zh: 对，审判体系。

segments.en: Alright.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So, what did you think of the story?
segments.zh: 那么，你对这个故事有什么看法？

segments.en: Did you like it?
segments.zh: 你喜欢吗?

segments.en: I really liked it.
segments.zh: 我真的很喜欢它。

segments.en: I thought it was really spooky and I thought that it built up well.
segments.zh: 我觉得它真的很吓人，而且铺垫得很好。

segments.en: But I really also like the imagery.
segments.zh: 但我也很喜欢其中的意象。

segments.en: We talked about, or we haven't talked about this yet, but he describes his great aunt, the character describes his great aunt as being spread out like the Vitruvian man.
segments.zh: 我们刚才说过——其实还没说到——故事中的人物形容自己的姑婆，四肢像《维特鲁威人》那样摊开。

segments.en: So, you have this image of her arms spread out and her legs spread out.
segments.zh: 所以，你脑海里就有她双臂张开、双腿张开的样子。

segments.en: You know that picture that da Vinci did of a human being and it's like an anatomy and it's in a circle and you can see the legs and the arms.
segments.zh: 你知道达·芬奇画的那个人体图吧，像是一幅解剖图，人画在一个圆圈里，可以看到张开的腿和胳膊。

segments.en: That's just so really like a powerful visual image.
segments.zh: 这真的是一个很有冲击力的视觉意象。

segments.en: Yeah, you can imagine her laying on the bed in this position, right?
segments.zh: 是的，你可以想象她在这个位置上躺在床上，对吧？

segments.en: Yeah, it is pretty scary.
segments.zh: 是的，这很可怕。

segments.en: What about you?
segments.zh: 你呢？

segments.en: Have you ever had any close encounters with the supernatural or ghosts or goblins or something like this?
segments.zh: 你有没有近距离遇到过超自然现象、鬼魂、小妖怪，或者类似的东西？

segments.en: No, personally I've never had any experiences like that and I tend to not believe those stories but maybe if this had happened to someone I knew I'd be a little bit more skeptical or less skeptical.
segments.zh: 没有，我个人从来没遇到过这种事，通常也不太相信这些故事。不过如果事情发生在我认识的人身上，我可能会更怀疑——或者说，没那么怀疑。

segments.en: What about when they have those documentaries or those recordings of strange voices or appearances like these old castles in England or stuff like that?
segments.zh: 那你怎么看那些纪录片，或者录下来的奇怪声音、显灵画面，比如英国古堡里的那些？

segments.en: What do you think?
segments.zh: 你觉得怎么样？

segments.en: I love those shows.
segments.zh: 我喜欢那些节目。

segments.en: I just watched one and it was about a haunted house.
segments.zh: 我刚看了一个，是关于一所鬼屋。

segments.en: There was a woman who used a Ouija board and it let a demon out and the demon possessed the girl and they called in a priest and the priest had to like exorcise the demon from the little girl and the house was haunted and it was hurting people and it was like possessing people.
segments.zh: 有个女人用了通灵板，放出了一只恶魔，恶魔附在女孩身上。他们请来一位神父，神父得把恶魔从小女孩体内驱走。那栋房子也闹鬼，会伤人，还会附在人身上。

segments.en: Wow, it sounds like a movie.
segments.zh: 哇，听起来像电影。

segments.en: Yeah, it does but it was like a TV show on Discovery Channel and it was really, really fun.
segments.zh: 是的，确实如此，但它就像探索频道上的电视节目，真的非常有趣。

segments.en: I don't actually believe that a spirit could push someone down the stairs.
segments.zh: 我真的不相信灵魂可以将某人推下楼梯。

segments.en: I think that you trip and then you attribute it to a spirit.
segments.zh: 我觉得其实是你自己绊倒了，然后把它归咎于鬼魂。

segments.en: What about the Ouija board?
segments.zh: 通灵板怎么样？

segments.en: That's an interesting tool that many people say opens up portals and dimensions towards hell or spirits can come out and stuff like that.
segments.zh: 那是个有意思的工具，很多人说它能打开通往地狱的通道或异空间，让鬼魂之类的东西出来。

segments.en: Well, for those of you who don't know, the Ouija board is a board, like a piece of cardboard that has letters on it, letters and numbers.
segments.zh: 如果有人不知道，通灵板就是一块板子，像硬纸板那样，上面有字母和数字。

segments.en: You have this glass that you hold and once the spirit comes, it guides the glass to point out to names or places and you spell them.
segments.zh: 你用手扶着一个玻璃杯，等灵体来了，它就会引导杯子指向字母，拼出名字或地名。

segments.en: They're really popular with like 13-year-old girls who have these slumber parties and they use it and we always say, you know, who is she going to date and then it moves.
segments.zh: 这种东西很受十三岁左右、喜欢开睡衣派对的女孩欢迎。我们总会问：“她会和谁约会？”然后杯子就动起来了。

segments.en: But yeah, I believe in the power of the human mind so I think a lot of times even if we're not aware of it, we're the ones manipulating this.
segments.zh: 不过，我相信人的意念有很强的力量，所以很多时候，即使自己没意识到，其实也是我们在操控它。

segments.en: Or believing what we want to believe.
segments.zh: 或相信我们想相信的。

segments.en: Yeah, but what about you?
segments.zh: 是的，但是你呢？

segments.en: Are you superstitious?
segments.zh: 你迷信吗？

segments.en: Do you believe in ghosts?
segments.zh: 你相信鬼吗？

segments.en: I'm not superstitious.
segments.zh: 我不迷信。

segments.en: I don't know what to think about ghosts because I've actually had a couple of very strange encounters with the supernatural but I really wouldn't say, oh yeah, I believe in ghosts or I believe there are spirits that haven't been put to rest or they have unfinished business, you know, like in Casper or something like that.
segments.zh: 我不知道该怎么看待鬼魂，因为我确实遇到过几次很奇怪的超自然现象。但我也不会直接说：“对，我相信有鬼，或者有些灵魂还没安息，还有未了的心愿。”就像《鬼马小精灵》里那样。

segments.en: But once we were having dinner with my family in the house where we used to live and it was a very old house and we had a glass of water on the table and all of a sudden it started to move and to rotate across the table, the center of the table and we all saw it and no one was touching it.
segments.zh: 有一次，我们一家人在以前住的房子里吃晚饭。那房子很老，桌上放着一杯水，突然杯子开始一边转，一边从桌面上移动，经过桌子中央。我们全都看见了，而且根本没人碰它。

segments.en: So we all were pretty confused and nervous and then just kind of burst out in nervous laughter and we didn't really know what to make of it but it was very strange because it moved a good amount, it was like half of the table and it was spinning at the same time so it was very strange.
segments.zh: 我们都很困惑，也很紧张，后来忍不住紧张地笑起来，实在不知道怎么解释。特别奇怪的是，它移动了很远，差不多横穿了半张桌子，同时还在旋转，真是很古怪。

segments.en: Weird.
segments.zh: 真奇怪。

segments.en: So, things like this and, you know, in general Hispanic or Latin American culture are, they're very superstitious.
segments.zh: 像这样的事情，在西语文化或拉丁美洲文化中很常见，那里的迷信观念很深。

segments.en: They have a lot of beliefs in like magic or some people still say, are reluctant to give out a picture for example because of something like this in the story.
segments.zh: 他们相信很多魔法之类的东西。比如，有些人仍然不愿意把自己的照片给别人，就是怕发生故事里这样的事。

segments.en: Really?
segments.zh: 真的吗？

segments.en: They don't give out pictures to boyfriends or girlfriends or anyone because if you break up or something is to happen then they could do something with that picture and maybe hurt you.
segments.zh: 他们不把照片给男朋友、女朋友或任何人，因为一旦分手，或发生什么事，对方就可能拿照片做法来伤害你。

segments.en: Really?
segments.zh: 真的吗？

segments.en: So this idea that you have a likeness, like a picture or a doll or something, can you talk about that because I don't really know anything about it.
segments.zh: 就是说，只要有一个人的形象，比如照片、玩偶之类的东西，就能起作用。你能讲讲这个观念吗？因为我对此完全不了解。

segments.en: Having that means that you're able to like do something to that very person?
segments.zh: 有这个东西，就意味着你能对那个人做点什么？

segments.en: Yeah, yeah.
segments.zh: 对，对。

segments.en: Like, not necessarily like a voodoo doll, right?
segments.zh: 就像，不一定像巫毒娃娃，对吧？

segments.en: Where you see that you can put pins in it and then it would hurt someone.
segments.zh: 就是往里面扎针，然后就能伤害到那个人的那种。

segments.en: But people believe that pictures, for example, they capture your image and so if somebody has it and wants to do harm or black magic then they can use that as an instrument to get into you.
segments.zh: 人们相信，照片记录了你的形象，所以如果有人拿着它，想伤害你或施黑魔法，就能把它当成影响你的工具。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: The same as pieces of clothing or the same as hair and things like this.
segments.zh: 和一件衣服一样，或者和头发一样的东西。

segments.en: So that's why there are the shamans or the Indian witch doctors who do cleansing like this and people still actually go to them.
segments.zh: 所以才会有萨满或原住民巫医来做这种净化仪式，而且人们现在还真的会去找他们。

segments.en: People in the city still believe in these things and they'll go to a shaman and get themselves cleansed because they believe that their luck, they have really bad luck or they've been very, very sick for a long time and doctors can't figure out what it is.
segments.zh: 城里人也仍然相信这些。他们会去找萨满做净化，因为觉得自己运气特别差，或者病了很久，医生也查不出原因。

segments.en: They think it's because someone has cast a spell on them or is doing some black magic to them and they need to get it cleansed.
segments.zh: 他们认为，这是因为有人对自己下了咒或施了黑魔法，所以需要把这些东西清除掉。

segments.en: Oh, wow.
segments.zh: 哦，哇。

segments.en: So, yeah, it's really, really common.
segments.zh: 所以，是的，这真的非常普遍。

segments.en: But it's all part of the folklore and the heritage of the countries.
segments.zh: 但这都是民间传说和国家遗产的一部分。

segments.en: It's actually very, very interesting and some things are just really out there, really weird.
segments.zh: 其实非常非常有意思，有些东西真的很离奇、很古怪。

segments.en: Yeah?
segments.zh: 是吗？

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Well, a lot of it I think comes from indigenous beliefs mixing with Catholicism too, right?
segments.zh: 嗯，我认为其中很多也来自与天主教混合的土著信仰，对吧？

segments.en: Yeah, exactly.
segments.zh: 对，没错。

segments.en: Because a lot of South American countries and Latin American countries are very Catholic but they get kind of melded, these traditions with indigenous beliefs and then you have these crazy rituals and like...
segments.zh: 因为很多南美和拉丁美洲国家都深受天主教影响，但这些传统又和原住民信仰融合在一起，于是就出现了这些奇特的仪式之类的……

segments.en: We actually have a belief and it's very true that when somebody is completely in love with this girl and this girl is maybe not very nice or not very nice to that guy but he's still completely into her.
segments.zh: 我们确实有这样一种说法，而且这种情况也很常见：一个男人深深爱上一个女孩，女孩人不太好，或者对他不好，可他仍然对她死心塌地。

segments.en: So, there's this word that we say that he's been like underweared or something like that.
segments.zh: 所以我们有个说法，说他被'内裤咒'迷住了，或类似的话。

segments.en: And the reason behind this is that one of these rituals that I talked about is that the girl would make tea, right?
segments.zh: 这个说法的由来是，我刚才提到的一种仪式，就是女孩会泡茶，对吧？

segments.en: Would take a tea pot and in it would put her underpants, used underpants to make the tea water and then would serve it to the guy.
segments.zh: 她会拿一个茶壶，把自己穿过的内裤放进去，用来泡茶，然后把茶端给那个男人喝。

segments.en: So, the moment that he drank it, this was like a magic potion and then he would continuously be in love with her.
segments.zh: 他一喝下去，就像喝了魔药一样，从此会一直爱着她。

segments.en: Oh.
segments.zh: 哦。

segments.en: So, yeah, it's very strange.
segments.zh: 所以，是的，这很奇怪。

segments.en: That's gross.
segments.zh: 真恶心。

segments.en: Do people actually do that?
segments.zh: 人们真的这样做吗？

segments.en: No.
segments.zh: 不。

segments.en: It's not something that you do now but it's something that people knew about that used to be done way, way before.
segments.zh: 现在不会这样做了，但人们知道，很久很久以前曾经有人这样做。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So, people now...
segments.zh: 所以，现在的人...

segments.en: It's part of the language where you say that someone has been like...
segments.zh: 这已经成了语言的一部分，你会说某人被……

segments.en: Underweared or something like that.
segments.zh: '内裤咒'迷住了，或类似的说法。

segments.en: She cast a spell on him maybe what we would say.
segments.zh: 换成我们的话说，也许就是'她对他施了咒'。

segments.en: So, things like this that of course aren't really done anymore but still people make reference to it because we know it from our history that it's been done before.
segments.zh: 当然，这些事情现在基本没人做了，但人们还会提起，因为我们从历史中知道，以前确实有过这种做法。

segments.en: How cool.
segments.zh: 太酷了。

segments.en: Well, I'm really curious to know if our users have any similar stories or have any scary stories they want to tell.
segments.zh: 我很好奇，我们的用户有没有类似的经历，或者有没有想分享的恐怖故事。

segments.en: I bet they do.
segments.zh: 我敢肯定他们有。

segments.en: I'm sure they do.
segments.zh: 我相信他们有的。

segments.en: And this advanced media lesson is a great place for you to do that because we expect that a lot of advanced level learners are going to be listening to it and practicing your writing is really important.
segments.zh: 这期高级听力素材课很适合大家分享，因为我们预计会有很多高级学习者来听，而且练习写作非常重要。

segments.en: So, we hope that you'll put some comments on this lesson and of course ask us as many questions as you want.
segments.zh: 所以，希望大家在本课下面留言，当然，也欢迎尽情提问。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So, we'll see you guys there and have a happy Halloween.
segments.zh: 所以，我们会在那里见到你们，度过一个快乐的万圣节。

segments.en: Happy Halloween.
segments.zh: 万圣节快乐。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。
